newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says ASEAN may review Burma stance.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says ASEAN may review Burma stance.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday the Association of Southeast Asian Nations might review its policy of "constructive engagement" towards Burma after its renewed crackdown on democracy activists.

Ramos told his weekly news conference the consensus among ASEAN foreign ministers remained for the seven-nation group to eventually admit Burma as a member provided it made progress on trade and political reforms.
But ASEAN might review its policy, he said.

"The ASEAN leaders will have their summit in late November 1996 and maybe the matter can be reviewed at that stage," Ramos said. "But we're leaving this to the Burmese themselves to correct or to improve upon."
He was replying to a question on whether Rangoon's latest crackdown on followers of Burmese democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi might compel ASEAN to think twice.

Aung San Suu Kyi slipped out of a police cordon near her home on Wednesday and told reporters Burma's military rulers had arrested up to 800 members and supporters of her National League for Democracy (NLD) since last Thursday.
She said the junta's latest crackdown and its decision to bar access to her residence was expected and would help boost her legitimacy.
ASEAN has adopted a so-called policy of "constructive engagement" towards Burma calling for quiet persuasion rather than confrontation to bring about democratic reforms.

The group, which comprises Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand, Brunei and Vietnam, has resisted pressure from the United States and other Western governments to adopt a tougher stance.
"The ASEAN consensus to admit Burma into ASEAN in due time, meaning following the step-by-step accession process, still goes," Ramos said.
"But in the meantime the expectation that Burma will also fulfill the standards within ASEAN for liberalised trade, a democratic system, (is) also there," Ramos added.
The NLD won elections in 1988 which SLORC never recognised.
ASEAN has accepted Burma as observer in the organisation but has yet to act upon its application for membership. ASEAN diplomats earlier said Burma's accession to full membership might come in 1998.
A senior Philippine diplomat said the latest developments in Rangoon could impair Burma's chances of early entry to the ASEAN.
"It might delay ASEAN action on the application," said the diplomat, who asked not to be named.
"Membership is a political act, an exercise of policy and along this line any development which will intrude into this policy will affect the membership issue," he said.
The diplomat said he expected ASEAN to discuss recent events in Rangoon and Burma's application for membership at its senior officials on October 18-19 in Kuala Lumpur.
